CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Tanah Bumbu Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Head of Region hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Tanah Bumbu Regency. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the people's representative institution of Tanah Bumbu Regency Region. 5. Agency is a Regional Apparatus that organizes government affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection. 6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in organizing government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 7. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that Women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 8. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into men and Women. 9. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a Woman. 10. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a Child who is still in the womb. 11. Child in conflict with the law (ABH) is a Child in conflict with the law, a Child who is a victim of a criminal act and a Child who is a witness to a criminal act. 12. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 13. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting Women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination. 15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security. 16. Toddler is a Child aged 0 (zero) to 5 (five) years, in the early stages of human development. 17. School-Age Child is a Child aged 6 (six) to 18 (eighteen) years. 18. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs for mental and religious guidance as well as clothing, food, shelter, health, education, physical, and social services are not properly met. 19. Child who is a victim of an act of Violence is a Child who experiences mistreatment such as being abused, humiliated, which endangers the Child physically, mentally and socially. 20. Child maltreatment is all forms of violence against children committed by those who should be responsible and/or those who have power over the child, who should be trusted, namely parents, close family, teachers, supervisors, law enforcement officers, caregivers and companions (World Health Organization). 21. Child in emergency situations is a Child who is in situations and conditions that endanger him/herself such as Children victims of riots, Children who become refugees, Children victims of natural disasters and Children in armed conflict. 22. Child in conflict with the law is a Child in conflict with the law, a Child victim of a criminal act, and a Child who is a witness to a criminal act. 23. Child of isolated indigenous community is a Child who lives in a situation of isolation where they cannot access basic needs. 24. Economically exploited Child is a Child who is forced and/or deceived to be employed by parents or others without being paid or being paid. 25. Sexually exploited Child is the use of a Child for sexual purposes with cash or other forms of compensation between the Child, buyer of sexual services, intermediary or agent and other parties who profit from the sexual trade of the Child. 26. Child who is a victim of Napza abuse is a Child who suffers from dependence on Napza caused by Napza abuse, either by their own will or because of encouragement or coercion by others. 27. Child with special needs is a Child who experiences physical and/or mental disabilities that interfere with growth and development in accordance with the stages of Child development. 28. Child victim of maltreatment is a Child who receives treatment that is not in accordance with the rights of the Child. 29. Village is a legal Community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage Government affairs, the interests of the local Community, based on Community initiative, rights of origin, and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 30. Child in need of Special Protection is a Child in emergency situations, a Child in conflict with the law, a Child from an isolated indigenous community, a Child who is economically and/or sexually exploited, a Child victim of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other active substance (Napza) abuse, a Child victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, a Child victim of physical and/or psychological Violence, a Child with special needs, and a Child victim of maltreatment and neglect. 31. Child Trafficking is a criminal act or action that meets one or more elements of recruitment, transfer, handover of a Child using Violence or threat of violence, fraud, kidnapping, confinement, abuse of power, exploitation of vulnerable positions or debt bondage for the purpose of and/or resulting in exploiting the Child. 32. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, Community, government/Regional Government, and the state.

Article 43

1. Every Child who is a victim of physical and/or psychological Violence as referred to in Article 36 letter g shall receive rehabilitation services both physical and psychosocial.
2. Forms of protection for Children who are victims of acts of Violence include basic social services, education, religious guidance, health services, psychological counseling and/or psychotherapy, legal assistance, recreational and educational activities and empowerment of parents of Children who are victims of acts of violence.
3. Every person and/or any party is prohibited from committing acts of Violence against Children.

Article 12

The Regional Government provides Women Protection in the form of:
a. prevention of Violence against Women;
b. provision of services for Women victims of Violence requiring Regional level coordination; and
c. strengthening and development of institutions providing Women Protection services.

CHAPTER VII SAFE HOUSES

Article 46

1. Women and Children who are victims of Violence who require ongoing treatment have the right to stay in a safe house.
2. The safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) shall provide a temporary safe place or shelter for victims of Violence until their rights are restored.
3. The operation and management of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Apparatus that performs functions in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
4. Further provisions regarding the operation of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 45

1. Special Protection for Children who are victims of mistreatment and neglect as referred to in Article 36 letter i shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment and rehabilitation.
2. Every person and/or any party is prohibited from placing, allowing, involving, ordering the involvement of Children in situations of mistreatment and neglect as referred to in paragraph (1).

CHAPTER VI

CHILD PROTECTION

Part One

General

Article 25

1. Rescue actions as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter b shall be carried out if based on the results of identification it is known that the safety of the Child is threatened.
2. Actions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by removing the Child from the threatening situation and environment.
3. The SKPD in charge of Child Protection shall carry out rescue actions and coordinate with the Police/Civil Service Police Unit.

Article 40

1. Special Protection for Children who are exploited economically and/or sexually as referred to in Article 36 letter d shall be carried out through:
a. prevention of Children from supervision utilized by certain parties as objects of exploitation;
b. dissemination and/or socialization of laws and regulations related to Protection of Children who are exploited economically and/or sexually;
c. monitoring, reporting and imposition of sanctions; and
d. involving various government agencies, companies, trade unions, NGOs, and the Community in the elimination of exploitation of Children.
2. Every person and/or any party is prohibited from conducting economic and/or sexual exploitation of Children as referred to in paragraph (1).

Article 29

Legal assistance/expert witness services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter d number 3 include:
a. ensuring that the Child is accompanied by legal counsel; and
b. facilitating assistance to Child victims of violence, both in the examination process in court proceedings and outside court proceedings.

Part Eight

Protection of Children Requiring Special Protection

Article 41

1. Special Protection for Children who are victims of narcotics abuse including aromatic glue and the like that can cause hallucinatory effects and the like as referred to in Article 36 letter e, and involved in the use, production and distribution thereof, shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation efforts by the Regional Government and the Community.
2. Every person and/or any party is prohibited from deliberately placing, allowing, involving, ordering the involvement of Children in the abuse, production and distribution of narcotics, aromatic glue and the like as referred to in paragraph (1).

Article 2

Point a
What is meant by "respect for human rights is that the protection and empowerment of women is carried out as a manifestation of respect for women as part of Human Rights.

Point b
What is meant by "gender equality" is one of the rights as a human being, the right to live with dignity, free from fear and free to determine life choices is not only intended for men, women also have the same rights in essence.

Point c
What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment towards Children by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups, and the condition of the Child.

Point d
What is meant by "justice and legal certainty is that in implementing the protection and empowerment of women it is based on justice and legal certainty of equality between men and women.

Point e
What is meant by "benefit" is providing the widest possible benefit for children and women for the interests of society, nation and state.

Point f
What is meant by "participatory" is that every member of society is encouraged to play an active role in the decision-making process and implementation of child protection and women's empowerment, either directly or indirectly.

Point g
What is meant by "the best interests of the Child" is that in all actions concerning Children carried out by the Regional Government, parents/family, and the Community, the best interests of the Child must be the primary consideration.
Point h What is meant by "accountability" is a principle that requires that every activity and final result of state administration activities must be accountable to the community and the people as holders of the highest sovereignty of the state in accordance with the provisions of applicable legislation.

Point i What is meant by "gender responsive" is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers to achieve gender equality.

CHAPTER VI

CHILD PROTECTION

Part One

General

Article 42

1. Special Protection for Children who are victims of kidnapping, sale and trafficking as referred to in Article 36 letter f shall be carried out through supervision, protection, prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and reintegration efforts by the Regional Government and the Community.
2. To implement prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government together with the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Courts, Community, NGOs and Social Organizations shall take steps in the form of:
a. conducting socialization and/or campaigns on the prevention, handling and elimination of Child Trafficking practices;
b. implementing cooperation with other Regions as well as with other countries through bilateral or multilateral cooperation in accordance with the laws and regulations.
3. Protection for Children who are victims of Child Trafficking shall be implemented through Shelters and/or other Child Protection Institutions, through referrals from government agencies or the Community.
4. Every Child who is a victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, has the right to obtain treatment and rehabilitation both physical, psychological and reintegration in the family environment as well as the Community.

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Point a
What is meant by "respect for human rights is that the protection and empowerment of women is carried out as a manifestation of respect for women as part of Human Rights.

Point b
What is meant by "gender equality" is one of the rights as a human being, the right to live with dignity, free from fear and free to determine life choices is not only intended for men, women also have the same rights in essence.

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment towards Children by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups, and the condition of the Child.

Point d
What is meant by "justice and legal certainty is that in implementing the protection and empowerment of women it is based on justice and legal certainty of equality between men and women.

Point e
What is meant by "benefit" is providing the widest possible benefit for children and women for the interests of society, nation and state.

Point f
What is meant by "participatory" is that every member of society is encouraged to play an active role in the decision-making process and implementation of child protection and women's empowerment, either directly or indirectly.

Point g
What is meant by "the best interests of the Child" is that in all actions concerning Children carried out by the Regional Government, parents/family, and the Community, the best interests of the Child must be the primary consideration.

Article 42

Article 47

1. Village Government shall implement Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the Village.

Article 40

1. Special Protection for Children who are exploited economically and/or sexually as referred to in Article 36 letter d shall be carried out through:
a. prevention of Children from supervision utilized by certain parties as objects of exploitation;
b. dissemination and/or socialization of laws and regulations related to Protection of Children who are exploited economically and/or sexually;
c. monitoring, reporting and imposition of sanctions; and
d. involving various government agencies, companies, trade unions, NGOs, and the Community in the elimination of exploitation of Children.
2. Every person and/or any party is prohibited from conducting economic and/or sexual exploitation of Children as referred to in paragraph (1).

Article 24

1. Identification and receipt of complaints/reports as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter a include:
a. ensuring the readiness of complaint services for Child Protection issues;
b. following up on information or complaints/reports received regarding Child Protection issues; and
c. identifying the type of problem, needs, and handling plan.
2. The SKPD in charge of Child Protection affairs must identify problems and receive complaints/reports.

Article 21

1. The Regional Government shall carry out Child Protection in the Region.
2. Child Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be through the Protection of Children's Rights.
3. Children's Rights as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be guided by the provisions of Tanah Bumbu Regency Regional Regulation Number 11 of 2021 concerning the Implementation of Child-Friendly Regency (Tanah Bumbu Regency Regional Gazette of 2021 Number 11, Supplement to Tanah Bumbu Regency Regional Gazette Number 126).

Article 26

1. Placement of Children in temporary shelters as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter c shall be carried out if based on the results of identification it is known that:
a. the safety of the Child is threatened;
b. the Child has no family/caregiver or guardian; and
c. the Child cannot be reunited with family/caregiver/guardian and/or the Community.
2. Placement as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out for a certain period of time while the Child receives recovery services and/or until the family/caregiver/guardian is deemed to have the readiness to care for and protect the Child.
3. In the placement as referred to in paragraph (2), the Child shall receive services for the fulfillment of basic needs and psychosocial assistance.
4. The SKPD in charge of social affairs must organize temporary shelters.

Article 42

1. Special Protection for Children who are victims of kidnapping, sale and trafficking as referred to in Article 36 letter f shall be carried out through supervision, protection, prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and reintegration efforts by the Regional Government and the Community.
2. To implement prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government together with the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Courts, Community, NGOs and Social Organizations shall take steps in the form of:
a. conducting socialization and/or campaigns on the prevention, handling and elimination of Child Trafficking practices;
b. implementing cooperation with other Regions as well as with other countries through bilateral or multilateral cooperation in accordance with the laws and regulations.
3. Protection for Children who are victims of Child Trafficking shall be implemented through Shelters and/or other Child Protection Institutions, through referrals from government agencies or the Community.
4. Every Child who is a victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, has the right to obtain treatment and rehabilitation both physical, psychological and reintegration in the family environment as well as the Community.

Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination. 15. Child who is a victim of an act of Violence is a Child who experiences mistreatment such as being abused, humiliated, which endangers the Child physically, mentally and socially. 20. Child of isolated indigenous community is a Child who lives in a situation of isolation where they cannot access basic needs. 24. Economically exploited Child is a Child who is forced and/or deceived to be employed by parents or others without being paid or being paid. 25. Child Trafficking is a criminal act or action that meets one or more elements of recruitment, transfer, handover of a Child using Violence or threat of violence, fraud, kidnapping, confinement, abuse of power, exploitation of vulnerable positions or debt bondage for the purpose of and/or resulting in exploiting the Child. 32. CHAPTER VII SAFE HOUSES

Article 46

1. Women and Children who are victims of Violence who require ongoing treatment have the right to stay in a safe house.
2. The safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) shall provide a temporary safe place or shelter for victims of Violence until their rights are restored.
3. The operation and management of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Apparatus that performs functions in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
4. Further provisions regarding the operation of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 26

1. Placement of Children in temporary shelters as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter c shall be carried out if based on the results of identification it is known that:
a. the safety of the Child is threatened;
b. the Child has no family/caregiver or guardian; and
c. the Child cannot be reunited with family/caregiver/guardian and/or the Community.

4. The SKPD in charge of social affairs must organize temporary shelters.

Article 42

Article 47

Article 2

Point a
What is meant by "respect for human rights is that the protection and empowerment of women is carried out as a manifestation of respect for women as part of Human Rights.

Point b
What is meant by "gender equality" is one of the rights as a human being, the right to live with dignity, free from fear and free to determine life choices is not only intended for men, women also have the same rights in essence.

Point c
What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment towards Children by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups, and the condition of the Child.

Point d
What is meant by "justice and legal certainty is that in implementing the protection and empowerment of women it is based on justice and legal certainty of equality between men and women.

Point e
What is meant by "benefit" is providing the widest possible benefit for children and women for the interests of society, nation and state.

Point f
What is meant by "participatory" is that every member of society is encouraged to play an active role in the decision-making process and implementation of child protection and women's empowerment, either directly or indirectly.

Point g
What is meant by "the best interests of the Child" is that in all actions concerning Children carried out by the Regional Government, parents/family, and the Community, the best interests of the Child must be the primary consideration.
Point h What is meant by "accountability" is a principle that requires that every activity and final result of state administration activities must be accountable to the community and the people as holders of the highest sovereignty of the state in accordance with the provisions of applicable legislation.

Point i What is meant by "gender responsive" is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers to achieve gender equality.

What is meant by "participatory" is that every member of society is encouraged to play an active role in the decision-making process and implementation of child protection and women's empowerment, either directly or indirectly.

Point g
What is meant by "the best interests of the Child" is that in all actions concerning Children carried out by the Regional Government, parents/family, and the Community, the best interests of the Child must be the primary consideration.
Point h What is meant by "accountability" is a principle that requires that every activity and final result of state administration activities must be accountable to the community and the people as holders of the highest sovereignty of the state in accordance with the provisions of applicable legislation.

Point i What is meant by "gender responsive" is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers to achieve gender equality.

Article 42

Article 46

4. Further provisions regarding the operation of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Child in emergency situations is a Child who is in situations and conditions that endanger him/herself such as Children victims of riots, Children who become refugees, Children victims of natural disasters and Children in armed conflict. 22. Child in conflict with the law is a Child in conflict with the law, a Child victim of a criminal act, and a Child who is a witness to a criminal act. 23. Child of isolated indigenous community is a Child who lives in a situation of isolation where they cannot access basic needs. 24. Economically exploited Child is a Child who is forced and/or deceived to be employed by parents or others without being paid or being paid. 25. Sexually exploited Child is the use of a Child for sexual purposes with cash or other forms of compensation between the Child, buyer of sexual services, intermediary or agent and other parties who profit from the sexual trade of the Child. 26. Child who is a victim of Napza abuse is a Child who suffers from dependence on Napza caused by Napza abuse, either by their own will or because of encouragement or coercion by others. 27. Child with special needs is a Child who experiences physical and/or mental disabilities that interfere with growth and development in accordance with the stages of Child development. 28. Child victim of maltreatment is a Child who receives treatment that is not in accordance with the rights of the Child. 29. Village is a legal Community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage Government affairs, the interests of the local Community, based on Community initiative, rights of origin, and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 30. Child in need of Special Protection is a Child in emergency situations, a Child in conflict with the law, a Child from an isolated indigenous community, a Child who is economically and/or sexually exploited, a Child victim of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other active substance (Napza) abuse, a Child victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, a Child victim of physical and/or psychological Violence, a Child with special needs, and a Child victim of maltreatment and neglect. 31. Child Trafficking is a criminal act or action that meets one or more elements of recruitment, transfer, handover of a Child using Violence or threat of violence, fraud, kidnapping, confinement, abuse of power, exploitation of vulnerable positions or debt bondage for the purpose of and/or resulting in exploiting the Child. 32. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, Community, government/Regional Government, and the state.

Article 8

The Regional Government has the authority to:
a. institutionalize Gender Mainstreaming;
b. conduct Women Empowerment in the political, legal, social and economic fields in community organizations; and
c. strengthen and develop institutions providing Women Empowerment services.

Article 21

1. The Regional Government shall carry out Child Protection in the Region.
2. Child Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be through the Protection of Children's Rights.
3. Children's Rights as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be guided by the provisions of Tanah Bumbu Regency Regional Regulation Number 11 of 2021 concerning the Implementation of Child-Friendly Regency (Tanah Bumbu Regency Regional Gazette of 2021 Number 11, Supplement to Tanah Bumbu Regency Regional Gazette Number 126).
